headline: How do I know if my property can have a guest home?
articleBody:
Considering adding a guest home? That’s fantastic! Many people in San Diego are realizing the potential of these flexible spaces. But before you get too far into design dreams, it’s super important to figure out if your property is actually a good fit. It’s not as simple as just having enough backyard space; there are some key things you’ll want to look into.

First up, zoning. Your property needs to be properly zoned for an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) or whatever legal classification your guest home will fall under. Different parts of San Diego County—like the City of San Diego versus unincorporated areas—have their own specific rules. These rules dictate things like how many units you can have, lot coverage, and density. 

Next, consider the physical aspects. Do you have adequate space for the actual structure, including required setbacks from property lines and other buildings? What about utility access? You'll need connections for water, sewer, and electricity. Sometimes, upgrading these systems can be a significant part of the project. Also, think about access for construction and future use; how will people get to it? 

Finally, it's all about local regulations and permits. This can be the trickiest part, as tiny homes and ADUs have unique considerations. We've spent years working with local agencies, understanding the nuances of these requirements across San Diego. It's worth getting a professional property assessment early on. It can save you a lot of headaches and ensure your guest home project is feasible, legal, and smoothly executed. We can help you with that initial property assessment to see what's possible!
